title: Triggering a re-render by changing vue state resets hierarchical menu
body:
### 🐛 Current behavior

When using a hierarchical menu, a vue triggered re-render resets it and performs a new search. This only seems to happen for hierarchical menus, though I have only compared against refinement lists at the moment. Refinement lists also get added to the browser url after triggering the re-render.

### 🔍 Steps to reproduce

1. Create a Vue Instantsearch component with a hierarchical menu
3. Add any component that changes the state and triggers a vue rerender
4. Select something in the hierarchical menu
5. Trigger a rerender, e.g. by clicking a button that changes the state
6. The hierarchical menu gets reset, without mapping the router state again### Live reproduction

https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/zealous-meadow-97dkdc

### 💭 Expected behavior

The current ui state should be retained, regardless of a vue re-render.

### Package version

vue-instantsearch@4.19.13 vue@2.7.16 typesense-instantsearch-adapter@2.8.0 (I am using typesense here, but that should not make a difference)

### Operating system

_No response_

### Browser

_No response_

comments.body: For reference, I am using a skeleton component inside the `ais-instant-search`, because I have no access to SSR. I only want the skeleton to show on initial page load, hence I am triggering a re-render when changing the `showSkeleton` ref after initial display of the results.
I noticed that this is not related to routing, sorry for the overcomplicated example. Re-rendering simply resets the hierarchical menu ui state. Updated the description and example.
This is likely related to the usage of inline arrays in props. They are not comparable and thus reset. If you put them in Vue data instead the problem will be gone.
